result.title: DINO-KNN: Training-Free Multiclass In-Context Segmentation via Nearest Neighbors
result.summary: In-context segmentation (ICS) segments a target image given a few annotated reference images. Recent training-free methods built on frozen foundation models segment one class at a time and gain little from additional references. We study the multiclass, multi-reference setting and ask how far a simple joint decision rule can go. We introduce DINO-KNN, which stores every labeled reference patch of a frozen DINOv3 encoder in a single memory and labels each target patch by a distance-weighted vote of its k nearest neighbors. All classes are predicted in a single pass, with one label per pixel, without training or a mask decoder. We evaluate on eight datasets, four natural and four medical, with R=1 to 15 reference images and three reference seeds. DINO-KNN achieves the best average mIoU at every R; it is the best method on six of the eight datasets from R=3 and on seven of the eight from R=7. Its accuracy continues to grow with the number of references, from 37.8 mIoU at R=1 to 56.2 at R=15, while the strongest baseline, INSID3, rises from 36.1 to 42.9. DINO-KNN is also 2.1x faster than INSID3. The code will be made public.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DINO-KNN：冻结 DINOv3 编码器下把所有参考图像 patch 存入单一记忆，目标 patch 由 k 近邻距离加权投票一次性完成多类分割，无需训练或 mask 解码器，并在八个数据集、R=1–15 上验证随参考数增加而持续提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「参考 patch 记忆 + 近邻投票 + 单次多类联合决策」可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、外部记忆读取与多假设标签分配的做法，但不涉及 latent 状态生成或推理轨迹，联系限于检索式决策机制。
